statement: Under the unchanged open-neighborhood definitions for finite simple connected graphs: (i) a pendant vertex and diameter two force its support to be universal, so no graph also has domination number two and Theorem 4.2 is vacuous; Lemma 4.1's initial minimality step is valid, but its later claim that a vertex at distance two dominates the pendant is invalid, while the remaining diameter arguments are unnecessary; (ii) among graphs with a pendant vertex, diameter three, and domination number two, the assertion gamma_t=2 is false first at order six, where exactly two isomorphism classes fail, with canonical graph6 strings E@V_ and EBYg, and both have gamma_t=3; (iii) independent-part vertex multiplication preserves total domination number, but the Petersen graph has gamma_t=4 rather than the paper's printed value 6, so the actual family H conclusion is gamma_t in {3,4}, with value 3 on the C5 and G0 branches and 4 on the Petersen branch. The instruction in source.md to preserve the value 6 is incompatible with its instruction not to change the definitions: accepting 6 counterfactually would propagate {3,6}, but does not repair the actual graph theorem.
contribution: A complete definition-preserving audit and repair of the frozen three-part problem: a shortest vacuity proof and corrected line audit, an exact least-order two-class counterexample atlas verified by exhaustive unlabeled and all-labeled enumeration, and a two-sided blow-up-invariance proof combined with an exact correction of the Petersen base value. No priority claim is made for the elementary Petersen computation or the finite atlas; the targeted literature comparison remains bounded as documented in problem.md.
